title: When using pandas.merge or pandas.join, the parameters on, how and validate should be provided
description: When using pandas.merge() or pandas.join() methods, the parameters 'on', 'how', and 'validate' should be explicitly provided to make the merge behavior clear and prevent unexpected results. Omitting these parameters can lead to implicit behavior that may not be obvious to other developers and can cause bugs when data changes.
message: When using pandas.merge or pandas.join, the parameters on, how and validate should be provided

impact.maintainability: High impact on code clarity and preventing merge-related bugs
impact.reliability: Medium impact on preventing unexpected data merge behavior

recommendation: Always explicitly specify the 'on', 'how', and 'validate' parameters when using pandas merge() or join() operations to make the intended behavior clear.

noncompliant.code:
import pandas as pd

df1 = pd.DataFrame({'key': ['A', 'B'], 'value1': [1, 2]})
df2 = pd.DataFrame({'key': ['A', 'C'], 'value2': [3, 4]})

# Missing 'on', 'how', and 'validate' parameters
result = df1.merge(df2)  # Unclear merge behavior

import pandas as pd

df1 = pd.DataFrame({'value1': [1, 2]}, index=['A', 'B'])
df2 = pd.DataFrame({'value2': [3, 4]}, index=['A', 'C'])

# Missing 'how' and 'validate' parameters
result = df1.join(df2)  # Unclear join behavior

import pandas as pd

df1 = pd.DataFrame({'key': ['A', 'B'], 'value1': [1, 2]})
df2 = pd.DataFrame({'key': ['A', 'C'], 'value2': [3, 4]})

# Only 'on' specified, missing 'how' and 'validate'
result = df1.merge(df2, on='key')

import pandas as pd

df1 = pd.DataFrame({'key': ['A', 'B'], 'value1': [1, 2]})
df2 = pd.DataFrame({'key': ['A', 'C'], 'value2': [3, 4]})

# Using pandas.merge function without explicit parameters
result = pd.merge(df1, df2)

compliant.description: Proper merge with all parameters specified
compliant.code:
import pandas as pd

df1 = pd.DataFrame({'key': ['A', 'B'], 'value1': [1, 2]})
df2 = pd.DataFrame({'key': ['A', 'C'], 'value2': [3, 4]})

# All parameters explicitly specified
result = df1.merge(df2, on='key', how='inner', validate='one_to_one')

compliant.description: Proper join with all parameters specified
compliant.code:
import pandas as pd

df1 = pd.DataFrame({'value1': [1, 2]}, index=['A', 'B'])
df2 = pd.DataFrame({'value2': [3, 4]}, index=['A', 'C'])

# All parameters explicitly specified
result = df1.join(df2, how='outer', validate='one_to_one')

compliant.description: Using pandas.merge function with explicit parameters
compliant.code:
import pandas as pd

df1 = pd.DataFrame({'key': ['A', 'B'], 'value1': [1, 2]})
df2 = pd.DataFrame({'key': ['A', 'C'], 'value2': [3, 4]})

# Using pandas.merge with all required parameters
result = pd.merge(df1, df2, on='key', how='left', validate='many_to_one')

compliant.description: Complex merge with multiple keys and validation
compliant.code:
import pandas as pd

df1 = pd.DataFrame({'key1': ['A', 'B'], 'key2': [1, 2], 'value1': [10, 20]})
df2 = pd.DataFrame({'key1': ['A', 'C'], 'key2': [1, 3], 'value2': [30, 40]})

# Explicit parameters with multiple keys
result = df1.merge(df2, on=['key1', 'key2'], how='outer', validate='one_to_many')

why_is_this_an_issue: When merge() or join() operations are performed without explicit parameters, pandas uses default behaviors that may not be obvious: (1) Default merge behavior can lead to unexpected results when data structure changes, (2) Missing 'how' parameter defaults to 'inner' join which may silently exclude data, (3) Missing 'validate' parameter can hide data quality issues like duplicate keys, (4) Implicit behavior makes code harder to understand and maintain, (5) Can lead to subtle bugs when datasets evolve over time, (6) Makes debugging more difficult when merge results are unexpected.

how_to_fix.description: Identify all pandas merge() and join() operations in your code
For merge() operations, explicitly specify the 'on' parameter to define which columns to merge on
Add the 'how' parameter to specify the type of join (inner, outer, left, right)
Include the 'validate' parameter to check for data quality (one_to_one, one_to_many, many_to_one, many_to_many)
For join() operations, specify the 'how' and 'validate' parameters explicitly
Test the merge/join operations to ensure they produce the expected results
Document the rationale for the chosen parameter values in comments if the logic is complex
